analysis.title: GS - Blaze - Brent Implied vs Realized Vol Ratio Shift - 29 Oct 2026
key_insights: The Brent implied vol/realized vol ratio has moved through three regimes since the conflict began. It opened near 1.28 and spiked to about 1.74 by March 6, when the market was paying up for protection well above realized daily moves.
The ratio fell to 0.53 on April 17, when realized vol ran nearly twice implied. The market underpriced the actual daily moves in Brent as it grew desensitized to escalation headlines.

The April period reflects an 'optimism selloff' dynamic. Brent fell 14.5% on Apr 1 and 13.7% on Apr 8 as the market treated each diplomatic signal as potentially decisive and was then whipsawed by renewed escalation.
In June and early July, implied and realized vol compressed together and the ratio hovered just below 1.0. Brent drifted toward $71-72/bbl as the market priced a tentative equilibrium.

The mid-July re-escalation pushed the ratio back above 1.0 on July 13, as Brent went from $72 to $100+. The current regime shows resilient price action with a rebuilding fear premium, visible first in flat price and later in vol.
Since September the ratio has climbed from about 1.03 to 1.96 on October 26, the highest since the first week of the conflict.
Brent's reaction to diplomatic headlines has shrunk. The Vance-Rezaee outreach produced only a -1.5% move, against -10%+ on equivalent headlines in March and April.
GS concludes the market has repriced its baseline geopolitical risk upward, so individual optimism events move prices less while the structural vol premium keeps rebuilding.
GS says the market has accepted $90-115/bbl Brent as the new operating range, with the distribution of outcomes skewed to the upside if the stalemate continues.

vol_and_positioning: Brent implied/realized vol ratio opened near 1.28 and spiked to about 1.74 by March 6.
The ratio troughed at 0.53 on April 17, with realized vol nearly twice implied.
In June and early July the ratio sat just below 1.0 as both implied and realized vol compressed.
The ratio went back above 1.0 on July 13 and rose from about 1.03 in September to 1.96 on October 26, the highest since the first week of the conflict.
The structural vol premium in Brent continues to rebuild, and the distribution of outcomes is skewed to the upside.

tension_points.bull_case: Structurally resilient Brent price action with a rebuilding vol premium. The market has accepted $90-115/bbl as the operating range, with outcomes skewed to the upside if the stalemate continues.
tension_points.bear_case: Diplomatic breakthroughs have produced large down days before, such as -14.5% on Apr 1 and -13.7% on Apr 8. The market now reacts far less to such headlines, though a decisive resolution could still reprice Brent.
